title: AI Frontiers in Trust and Safety  Combatting Multifaceted Harm on Tinder at Scale: Vibhor Kumar
talk_summary: A Tinder trust-and-safety engineer describes fine-tuning small open-source LLMs with LoRA/QLoRA adapters to classify policy violations, serving many adapters cheaply on one GPU via LoRAX, and gating inference with heuristics and cascades. The core transferable ideas are cheap per-task fine-tuned classifiers, confidence scores from output distributions, and heuristic/cascade gating to cut inference volume.

takeaways.what_they_do: Train adapters on smaller base models optimized for recall, and only call the larger base model adapter when the smaller model's score is high enough.
takeaways.evidence_quote: train adapters on smaller base models optimizing for recall and only train only call the larger base model adapters when the smaller one gives a high enough score

takeaways.what_they_do: Only invoke the model on inputs that pass cheap heuristics (e.g., bios containing out-of-dictionary words), skipping obvious non-candidates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can make predictions only on bios that contain some word that's not in a dictionary

takeaways.technique: Fine-tuned task-specific classifiers instead of API LLMs
takeaways.what_they_do: Fine-tune small open models per violation type rather than calling GPT-4 in production, gaining control over weights and output probability distributions for confidence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have access to the output probability distribution, which means uh we can use the confidence we can create essentially a confidence of the prediction
takeaways.numbers: near 100% recall on simpler tasks like social handle detection

takeaways.technique: LoRA adapter multiplexing on shared GPUs
takeaways.what_they_do: Serve thousands of small LoRA adapters on one GPU by batching adapters and requests, making marginal cost of a new adapter near zero.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the marginal cost of serving a new adapter on the same base model is virtually zero
takeaways.numbers: tens of QPS at ~100ms latency on A10 GPUs with 7B models

takeaways.technique: LLM-assisted dataset mining with human verification
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the largest LLM with prompting to mine candidate examples from internal data, then manually verify and fix labels, yielding hundreds-to-thousands of high-quality examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can then do a manual verification, fixing any mislabeled data, and making judgment calls where the label is more ambiguous

takeaways.what_they_do: Frame detection as classification/extraction so the model emits one or a few tokens, keeping time-to-prediction low versus free-form generation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: classification or extraction tasks require only uh exactly one token or a few tokens to output, which means our time to prediction is low
